mainTopic: A נזיר who discovers he was טמא: known versus hidden טומאת התהום, its source as a tradition, and whether the time of finding out matters
overview: The משנה teaches that if a נזיר already shaved and only then finds out he was טמא מת, a known טומאה cancels (סותר) his נזירות, but a hidden טומאת תהום does not. If he finds out before shaving, it cancels either way. A cave case illustrates this: a corpse floating openly is a known טומאה. For a corpse sunk in the cave floor, each person keeps his earlier חזקה. The גמרא asks for the source of the distinction. רבי אליעזר learns it from ״עליו״ (clear to him), and ריש לקיש learns it from 'a road far away' (out in the open). Two ברייתות raise difficulties: hidden means unknown to anyone in the world, and a hidden corpse under a road makes a person טמא for תרומה but not for נזיר or פסח. So the גמרא concludes that טומאת התהום is a received tradition. Next, רבי יוחנן says the line about finding out before shaving follows רבי אליעזר, who holds that shaving is required to finish the נזירות. Finally, רמי בר חמא asks whether a נזיר who became טמא during his days but found out only after they ended loses his days, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Known impurity versus hidden impurity after shaving
steps.stepSummary: A נזיר who shaved and then learned he was טמא: a known טומאה cancels his נזירות, a טומאת תהום does not. Before shaving, it cancels either way.
steps.simpleTranslation: A נזיר shaved to finish his נזירות, and afterward he found out that he had been impure. If it was a known impurity, his נזירות is cancelled. If it was an impurity of the depths that nobody knew about, it is not cancelled. If he found out before he shaved, his נזירות is cancelled in either case.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives its main rule: what happens when a נזיר finds out about a past טומאת מת only after he has already shaved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two things decide the outcome: whether the טומאה was known (ידועה) or hidden (תהום), and whether he found out before or after his גילוח. The leniency for hidden טומאה applies only after shaving. Before shaving, any טומאה is סותר.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who vowed to stay away from wine, haircuts and טומאת מת
He shaved, the final step that ends a נזירות
A known impurity that people were aware of
Impurity of the depths, from a hidden corpse nobody knew about
Cancels (literally 'knocks down'), so the נזירות days must be redone

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule shows that the הלכה sometimes treats a hidden, unknown טומאה more leniently than a known one, especially once a process like נזירות has already been completed.

phrases.english: MISHNA: A nazirite who shaved,
and it became known to him that he was impure,
if it was a known impurity, he negates his naziriteship,
and if it was impurity of the depths, he does not negate it.
phrases.notes: "The depths" means a hidden grave or corpse that nobody knew was there.

phrases.english: If he found out before he shaved,
either way, he negates it.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָזִיר שֶׁגִּילַּח, וְנוֹדַע לוֹ שֶׁהוּא טָמֵא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After גילוח, a known טומאה is סותר and a טומאת תהום is not. Before גילוח, both are סותר.

steps.title: The cave case: a floating corpse versus a sunken corpse
steps.stepSummary: The משנה illustrates the rule: a corpse floating at the cave's mouth makes him טמא, and the case of a corpse sunk in the cave floor is introduced.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? Someone went down to immerse in a cave, and a dead body was found floating at the mouth of the cave. He is impure. If it was found sunk into the ground of the cave...
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a real-life example to show what counts as known and what counts as hidden. It ends by setting up the sunken-corpse case, and the next line gives the ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A corpse floating openly at the cave entrance was visible, so it counts as a known טומאה and he is טמא. A corpse sunk into the cave's floor is the hidden kind. The משנה does not give that ruling yet; it first says the result depends on why he went down.

keyTerms.meaning: How so? (introduces an example)
To immerse in water for purification
A cave, here one with water used for immersion
Floating
Sunk, buried down

phrases.english: How so?
If he went down to immerse in a cave,

phrases.aramaic: וְנִמְצָא מֵת צָף עַל פִּי הַמְעָרָה
phrases.english: and a corpse was found floating at the mouth of the cave,
he is impure,
if it was found sunk into the ground of the cave,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the known and hidden categories from step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A visible, floating corpse is a known טומאה, so the person is טמא.

steps.title: For the sunken corpse, his earlier status decides
steps.stepSummary: With a sunken corpse, someone who went in to cool off stays טהור, and someone who went in to purify himself from טומאת מת stays טמא, because each keeps his חזקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he went down to cool off, he is pure. If he went down to purify himself from corpse impurity, he is impure. Because one who has the status of impure stays impure, and one who has the status of pure stays pure, since there is a basis for the matter.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes the sunken-corpse case. The answer depends on what his status was before he went into the water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he was already טהור (he only went in to cool off), the hidden corpse does not take away his status, so he stays טהור. If he was טמא and went in to become pure, the doubt does not let him out of his טומאה, so he stays טמא. The principle is חזקה: each person keeps the status he already had.

keyTerms.meaning: To cool off
To become pure
Presumed status, meaning we assume things stay as they were
There is a basis for the matter (literally 'the matter has legs')

steps.whatToRemember: With a hidden corpse, the person keeps his earlier status: a טהור person who went in to cool off stays טהור, and a טמא person who went in to purify himself stays טמא.
steps.confusionAlert: The person who went in 'to purify himself' was not made טמא by the corpse. He was already טמא, and because of the doubt his immersion does not help, so he simply stays טמא.

phrases.english: If he went down to cool off, he is pure.
If he went down to purify himself from corpse impurity, he is impure.
For one who has the presumed status of impure stays impure,
and one who has the presumed status of pure stays pure,
since there is a basis for the matter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ruling for the sunken-corpse case opened in step 2
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the case of a hidden corpse, each person keeps his prior חזקה: טהור stays טהור and טמא stays טמא.

steps.title: Where does the known versus hidden rule come from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the משנה's distinction between known and hidden טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: From where are these matters derived?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking for the source of the משנה's rule. This sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה treated known and hidden טומאה differently, but it did not say why. The גמרא wants a basis in the תורה for this difference.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that analyzes the משנה
From where are these matters derived? (asking for a source)

phrases.english: GEMARA: From where are these matters derived?
phrases.notes: He means the difference between known and hidden impurity from the משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the משנה's ruling
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for treating known טומאה differently from hidden טומאה

steps.title: רבי אליעזר learns it from the word "עליו"
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר derives from ״עליו״ in the פסוק about a נזיר that only a טומאה clear to the person cancels his נזירות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר said: the verse says, "And if any man shall die very suddenly beside him." The word "beside him" teaches that it must be clear to him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר answers the question by pointing to a word in the פסוק about a נזיר who becomes טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could have just said a person died. By adding ״עליו״ ("beside him" or "upon him"), it suggests the טומאה is something clearly connected to him and known. A hidden corpse that nobody knew about does not fit this description, so it is not סותר after shaving.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sage who gives the source
For the verse says
Beside him, or upon him
When it is clear to him

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אליעזר, the difference between known and hidden טומאה comes from ״עליו״: only a טומאה that is clear to him is סותר. ריש לקיש gives a different source in the next step, and step 10 concludes that the rule is really a tradition, with the פסוקים only as support.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer said,
that the verse states:
"And if any man shall die beside him
very suddenly,"
"beside him" means when it is clear to him.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word ״עליו״ teaches that only a טומאה that is clear to the person (a known טומאה) is סותר.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי אליעזר proposes that known טומאה is סותר and hidden טומאה is not, based on the word ״עליו״. This derivation is later challenged in step 8, and the rule is reclassified as a tradition in step 10.

steps.title: ריש לקיש learns it from the word 'road'
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש derives the rule from the פסוק about פסח: טומאה is placed next to 'a road far away,' so like a road, the טומאה must be out in the open.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: The פסוק says, 'Who shall be impure due to a corpse or on a road far away.' The טומאה is like a road. Just as a road is out in the open, so too every טומאה must be out in the open.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives a different source than רבי אליעזר for the rule that only a known טומאה counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר learned the rule from ״עליו״ in the נזיר section. ריש לקיש uses the פסח section instead and compares the טומאה to the road listed next to it. A road is public and visible, so the טומאה must also be 'visible,' meaning known.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא of ארץ ישראל, the study partner of רבי יוחנן
Impure from a corpse
A road far away (from the פסח section)
Out in the open, known

steps.whyThisMatters: Now there are two possible sources for the rule. The next steps test which one fits the ברייתות.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
The verse states:
"Who shall be impure due to a corpse
phrases.notes: במדבר ט:י. This is the section about people who miss the קרבן פסח.

phrases.english: or on a road far away."
Like a road:
phrases.notes: Since the two are listed together in the פסוק, the טומאה is compared to the road.

phrases.english: just as a road is in the open,
so too every [impurity] is in the open.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the question in step 4, alongside רבי אליעזר's answer in step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From the comparison of טומאה to 'a road' in the פסח section: like a road, the טומאה must be in the open.

steps.title: A teaching defines hidden impurity as unknown to anyone in the world
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא: טומאת התהום is a corpse that not even one person at the end of the world knows about. If anyone knows, it is not טומאת התהום.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about what we learned: What is טומאת התהום? Any corpse that not even one person at the end of the world knows about. But if one person at the end of the world knows about it, it is not טומאת התהום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge by quoting a teaching that defines hidden טומאה. The actual question comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא sets a very strict standard: the טומאה is only 'hidden' if nobody anywhere knows of it. So it depends on whether anyone in the world knows, not on whether the נזיר himself knows.

keyTerms.meaning: But what about what we learned (opens a challenge from a source)
Impurity from a hidden, unknown corpse
Knows of it
The end of the world, anywhere at all

phrases.english: But what about that which we learned:
Which is impurity of the depths?
Any [corpse] that not even one person knows of
at the end of the world.
But if one person at the end of the world knows of it,
this is not impurity of the depths.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source that will be used to test the two derivations in steps 5 and 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two derivations of the hidden-טומאה rule (setup only)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The definition makes it depend on anyone in the world knowing, which will be measured against each derivation in the next step.

steps.title: The definition fits 'road' but not 'clear to him'
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא fits ריש לקיש's road comparison, but it is hard for רבי אליעזר: if the טומאה must be clear to the נזיר himself, why does it matter that a stranger far away knows?
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, according to the one who says 'like a road,' this is fine. But according to the one who says the טומאה must be clear to him, if one person at the end of the world knows about it, what difference does that make?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אליעזר: his source does not seem to match the ברייתא's definition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A road is public, so anything known to someone somewhere fits ריש לקיש's 'in the open.' רבי אליעזר's ״עליו״ talks about the נזיר's own knowledge, so a stranger's knowledge should not matter to him. Yet the ברייתא says it does.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, this works for one view (the next part is the problem)
Fine, it works
Clear to him
What of it? What difference does it make?

phrases.english: Granted, according to the one who says "like a road,"
phrases.notes: That is ריש לקיש from step 6.

phrases.english: it is fine.
But according to the one who says
[it must be] clear to him,
phrases.notes: That is רבי אליעזר's reading of ״עליו״ from step 5.

phrases.english: if one person at the end of the world knows of it,
what of it?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר כִּי דֶרֶךְ שַׁפִּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא from step 7 to challenge רבי אליעזר's derivation.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His source depends on the נזיר's own knowledge, but the ברייתא depends on whether anyone in the world knows.

steps.title: A second teaching treats תרומה differently from נזיר and פסח
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that someone who finds a corpse lying across a road is טמא for תרומה but טהור for נזיר and פסח. The גמרא asks what explains this difference.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, it was taught: Someone who finds a corpse lying across the width of a road is impure regarding תרומה, but pure regarding נזיר and bringing the קרבן פסח. What is the difference?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second difficulty: a teaching where the same hidden corpse makes someone impure for one thing and pure for others.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The corpse was hidden under the road, so the person passing could not have known about it. Yet for תרומה he is impure, while for נזיר and פסח he is pure. The גמרא asks what reason could explain this split.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore (adds another difficulty)
Across the full width of the road
The כהן's portion of produce, which must be eaten in purity
Bringing the קרבן פסח
What is the difference?

phrases.english: And furthermore, that which was taught:
One who finds a corpse lying
across the width of the road,
regarding תרומה, he is impure;
regarding a nazir and performing the Pesach, he is pure.
What is the difference?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second challenge on top of the one in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the hidden-טומאה rule comes from logic or a פסוק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same hidden corpse makes someone impure for תרומה but pure for נזיר and פסח, and the פסוקים give no clear reason for this split.

steps.title: Hidden impurity is a tradition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the law of טומאת התהום is not truly learned from the פסוקים. It is a tradition that was passed down.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the law of טומאת התהום is known by tradition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves both challenges by saying the rule comes from a tradition, not from either פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the rule is a tradition, its exact details come from the tradition itself. That explains why it depends on anyone in the world knowing, and why it applies to נזיר and פסח but not to תרומה. The פסוקים of רבי אליעזר and ריש לקיש are only extra support.

keyTerms.meaning: They learned it as a tradition

steps.whatToRemember: For a נזיר who already shaved, and for someone bringing the פסח, a hidden טומאת התהום does not count against him, but a known טומאה does. The details of טומאת התהום come from a tradition, not from the פסוקים, and the leniency does not apply to תרומה.
steps.confusionAlert: Here the word גמרא does not mean the Talmud. In גְּמָרָא גְּמִירִי לַהּ it means 'a received tradition.'

phrases.english: Rather, impurity of the depths
is learned as a tradition.
phrases.notes: So the פסוקים quoted earlier are only extra support, not the real source.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא טוּמְאַת הַתְּהוֹם גְּמָרָא גְּמִירִי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenges in steps 8 and 9 by changing what the source of the rule is.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: טומאת התהום is a received tradition. The פסוקים are only support, which explains its details, including why תרומה is treated differently.

steps.title: Who taught the line about finding out before shaving?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling about a נזיר who found out about the טומאה before shaving, and asks which תנא holds this view.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'If before he shaved, etc.' Which תנא is this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a line in the משנה and asks whose opinion it follows. This sets up רבי יוחנן's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said that if the נזיר learned of the hidden טומאה before he shaved, he loses his days. That suggests that until he shaves, he is still in the middle of his נזירות. Not every תנא agrees with that, so the גמרא wants to know who said it.

keyTerms.meaning: A sage of the משנה period. 'מאן תנא' means 'whose opinion is this?'
'Etc.' The גמרא quotes only the start of the line and expects you to know the rest.
He shaved. This is the shaving a נזיר does when his נזירות is complete.

phrases.english: "If before he shaved, etc."
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה. The full line says that if he found out before shaving, he loses his days, even for טומאת התהום.

phrases.english: Who is the tanna who taught this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After concluding that טומאת התהום is a tradition, the גמרא moves to another line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that finding out about the טומאה before shaving still makes the נזיר lose his days.

steps.title: It follows רבי אליעזר, who says shaving is required
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the משנה follows רבי אליעזר, who holds that the shaving is necessary to complete the נזירות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: This is רבי אליעזר, who says that shaving holds back the completion of the נזירות.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן identifies the author of the משנה: רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי אליעזר, a נזיר is not finished until he shaves. So if he finds out before shaving, he finds out while he is still a נזיר, and he loses his days. Someone who holds that shaving is not required would see him as already finished.

keyTerms.meaning: The shaving at the end of the נזירות.
Holds back. The נזירות is not complete without it.
An אמורא who answers the question here.

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's ruling that he loses his days if he finds out before shaving fits רבי אליעזר: without the shaving, the נזירות is not over yet.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
It is Rabbi Eliezer,
who says: shaving is indispensable.
phrases.notes: The נזירות isn't finished until he shaves, so before shaving he still counts as a נזיר.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הִיא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי אליעזר, who holds that shaving is necessary to complete the נזירות.

steps.title: Do we go by when he found out or when it happened?
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא asks about a נזיר who became טמא during his days but only found out after the days were complete.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא asked: If he became טמא during the days of his נזירות, and found out only after the days were complete, what is the law? Do we go by when he found out, and he found out after the days were complete? Or not?
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא raises a new question: what counts, the moment the טומאה happened or the moment he learned of it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The טומאה happened during the נזירות, which would normally make him lose his days. But he only found out after the days were done. If the law follows the moment he found out, he may not lose his days. If it follows the moment the טומאה happened, he loses them.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked. It introduces a question the גמרא is unsure about.
The completion of the days of the נזירות.
Knowing, or finding out.
'We go after...' It asks which factor decides the law.
'What is it?' This means: what is the law in this case?

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two times. The טומאה happened during the days. Only his knowing about it came after the days were done.

phrases.english: Rami bar Ḥama asked:
If he became impure during the full term
and it became known to him after the full term, what is the law?
phrases.notes: In this case he has finished the days but has not shaved yet.

phrases.english: Do we go according to the knowledge,
and this is knowledge after the full term,
or not?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the idea that finding out about the טומאה matters, and asks whether the time of finding out decides the law.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the law follows the time he found out or the time the טומאה actually happened.

steps.title: What is the question about? Losing his days
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference the question makes, and answers that it is about whether he loses his days.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for what is this asked? For whether he loses his days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes clear what רמי בר חמא's question is about: whether this נזיר has to start over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is not whether he is טמא. It is only whether he loses the days he has already kept. The גמרא sets this up so the discussion can go on.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And for what?' What difference does the question make?
To cancel, meaning the days of נזירות he already kept are lost.

phrases.english: And with regard to what?
With regard to negating?
phrases.notes: In other words, does he lose the days he already kept and have to start his נזירות over?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows down what רמי בר חמא's question is about.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which law depends on the question: whether he loses his days.
